note: Clin Path I Exam 1 key-trim (2026-09-25): these ENT key edits are LIVE in ent-pathophysiology-quiz*.html and the master forms but NOT yet in tools/clinpath_ent_sets.json or tools/clinpath_ent_pool.py (outside cp_* ownership). Apply each old->new as an exact string replacement in both files before any re-run of render_clinpath_ent.py, or the render will revert them.

edits.stem: Why does asymmetrical vestibular input produce a false sense of motion?
edits.old_key: The brain reads the mismatch between the two sides as movement
edits.new_key: The brain reads the mismatch as motion

edits.stem: Which demographic and inheritance profile fits otosclerosis?
edits.old_key: Young-to-middle-aged females, accelerated by pregnancy; 50% autosomal dominant

edits.stem: Why are nasal polyps classed as non-neoplastic?
edits.old_key: No new tissue is grown; existing mucosa becomes edematous
edits.new_key: No new tissue grows; the mucosa is edematous

edits.stem: What makes the middle ear vulnerable to the pressure changes behind otitis media?
edits.old_key: It is an air-filled space vented only by the Eustachian tube
edits.new_key: It vents only via the Eustachian tube

edits.stem: Which statement about bacterial tonsillitis and its abscess complication is accurate?
edits.old_key: Group A Streptococcus; asymmetric deviation with trismus
edits.new_key: Group A Streptococcus; asymmetry and trismus

edits.stem: Which structure separates the external ear from the middle ear?
edits.old_key: The tympanic membrane, which vibrates and passes energy to the ossicles
edits.new_key: The tympanic membrane, which vibrates the ossicles

edits.stem: Why does the vertigo of Meniere disease come in attacks rather than continuously?
edits.old_key: Pressure builds until micro-ruptures occur, then re-equilibrates

edits.stem: Which two ototoxic effects are reversible or symptom-limited rather than permanent?
edits.old_key: Furosemide on the strial potential; salicylate on prestin

edits.stem: Why does prolonged antibiotic use predispose to FUNGAL otitis externa?
edits.old_key: It removes the bacterial competition that normally limits fungal growth

edits.stem: What is the mechanism of Meniere disease?
edits.old_key: Defective endolymph resorption causing hydrops, ballooning the scala media until micro-ruptures occur
edits.new_key: Defective endolymph resorption causes hydrops until micro-ruptures occur

edits.stem: Why does anticoagulation favor POSTERIOR rather than anterior epistaxis?
edits.old_key: Posterior bleeding is driven by systemic vascular and clotting factors

edits.stem: Why does cerumen impaction cause conductive rather than sensorineural loss?
edits.old_key: It blocks the canal, so sound never reaches the conducting chain
edits.new_key: It blocks sound delivery down the canal

edits.stem: Which description fits vocal cord polyps, as distinct from nodules?
edits.old_key: Unilateral, soft and pedunculated on the middle third, after one severe strain
edits.new_key: Unilateral, soft, pedunculated; from one severe strain
edits.old_key_explanation: Correct. One event rather than chronic repetition, and the healing response is inflammatory rather than a callus. Site and laterality both differ from nodules.
edits.new_key_explanation: Correct. One event rather than chronic repetition, and the healing response is inflammatory rather than a callus. Polyps sit on the middle third, so site and laterality both differ from nodules.

edits.stem: Why are there three semicircular canals rather than one?
edits.old_key: They sit in three planes, so rotation in any direction is detected
edits.new_key: They cover three planes of rotation

edits.stem: What does it mean, structurally, for lymph nodes to be MATTED?
edits.old_key: They have lost their individual capsules and move as one mass
edits.new_key: They move together as one mass
edits.old_key_explanation: Correct. Matted nodes move together as one mass, and persistent rubbery or matted nodes in older adults require assessment to rule out lymphoma.
edits.new_key_explanation: Correct. Matted nodes have lost their individual capsules and move together as one mass, and persistent rubbery or matted nodes in older adults require assessment to rule out lymphoma.

edits.stem: Which features mark vertigo as PERIPHERAL rather than central?
edits.old_key: Sudden onset, horizontal or rotational nystagmus, fatigable, suppressed by visual fixation
edits.new_key: Sudden onset, horizontal-rotary nystagmus, fatigable, suppressed by fixation

edits.stem: Why does a lesion of cranial nerve VIII produce the same audiometric pattern as cochlear damage?
edits.old_key: Both sit beyond the conducting chain, so both give sensorineural loss
edits.new_key: Both lie beyond the conducting chain
edits.old_key_explanation: Correct. The category is defined by where the defect sits, not by which of the two structures failed.
edits.new_key_explanation: Correct. Both sit beyond the conducting chain, so both give sensorineural loss. The category is defined by where the defect sits, not by which of the two structures failed.
